title: Regularity of the new test boundary at retained Hilbert--Samuel levels
statement: Let $X\hookrightarrow M$ be a closed scheme of finite type over $\mathbf Q$ with $M$ smooth; no reducedness is assumed [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Define $h_{X,x}(n)=\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_{X,x}/\mathfrak m_x^{n+1})$, $\Lambda f(n)=\sum_{i=0}^n f(i)$ and $H_X(x)=\Lambda^{\operatorname{trdeg}_{\mathbf Q}\kappa(x)}h_{X,x}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-length, def-kun-transcendence-degree, def-weil-residue-field]. Suppose $H_X\le_{\rm lex}H_0$ at every point of $X$, in the lexicographic order of [def-trf-hilbert-samuel-invariant], and supply an actual presentation of $H_0$ and a finite admissible test sequence in the sense of [def-trf-hilbert-samuel-presentation], whose test boundary starts empty. Use strict transform of $X$ at admissible blowups and ordinary cartesian pullback at line and exceptional-intersection tests [def-nagata-strict-transform, def-nagata-global-blowup]. At prefix $j$ let $L_j=\Lambda^{r_j}H_0$, where $r_j$ counts line products. Then $H_{X_j}\le_{\rm lex}L_j$ everywhere. At every $x\in X_j$ with $H_{X_j}(x)=L_j$, the local equations of any subset of the distinct test-boundary hypersurfaces through $x$, in any order, form a regular sequence on $\mathcal O_{X_j,x}$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Here regular means that each equation acts injectively after quotienting by its predecessors and the final quotient is nonzero. Earlier-center ideals recorded before the presentation are excluded from this boundary. No assertion about irreducible components or their dimensions is made.

source.place: BMT arXiv:0905.3580v1, sections 5.2 and 6.2-6.3, initially empty test boundary; agent structural refinement of supported standard-basis test propagation. Supporting existing nodes: lem-per-hilbert-boundary-supported-certificates and lem-per-nonreduced-regular-hilbert-coefficients. Online source https://arxiv.org/html/0905.3580v1 read; archival PDF WANTED. No Stacks tag states this finite-test boundary assertion.

proof.text: Fix a finite sequence and work locally at its points. A supplied presentation identifies its cosupport after each prefix with the retained-level locus [def-trf-hilbert-samuel-presentation]; hence every admissible center is contained in that locus. At depth zero choose the actual nonreduced coefficient data at a point with $H_X=H_0$ using [lem-per-nonreduced-regular-hilbert-coefficients]. They have empty boundary and reference diagram $H_D=H_0$ by [lem-trf-jet-diagram-hilbert-control]. No replacement of the defining ideal by its radical is made. After shrinking the chart around that point, the equality locus of the extended function is exactly the coefficient order locus $S$ on $N$: the datum satisfies the five conditions at every point of $S$, so this is the first assertion of [lem-trf-formal-coefficient-transform-criterion]; and the datum's Taylor-dimension bound gives $H\le H_D$ on the chart. These are the hypotheses on the level and on $S$ which Step 2 needs for the first block. To initialize at points below $H_0$, observe that before the first admissible center affecting the germ all tests involve only independent line coordinates: their boundary blowup charts are smooth over the original germ by [lem-trf-coordinate-subspace-blowup-charts]. Thus these charts are smooth products of the original germ with the added number of variables; the jet formula gives $H_j=\Lambda^{r_j}H_X$ there. Summation preserves strict inequality, since at the first differing index its difference equals the original difference.

source.place: BMT arXiv:0905.3580v1 §§5.2,6.1–6.3,6.5–6.6, read at https://arxiv.org/html/0905.3580v1; BM2 Chapter III is the construction reference. Agent structural refinement; archival PDF WANTED. No Stacks tag states this coefficient-chart transport.

proof.text: Decompose the finite history into admissible blowups followed by strings of auxiliary tests. Inductively store the regular coefficient charts on the retained locus, their diagrams and whole-series multiplication and derivative certificates through the intervening auxiliary strings. Apply [lem-per-supported-exceptional-chart-packet] to each block. Its hypotheses are the coefficient datum from Step 1 or the preceding retained chart; its next center is in the equality locus by the presentation predicate. Its conclusion gives on the transformed support either a persistent strict rank witness or the actual ideal $(f_i')$, pure transverse homogeneous division, multiplication identities, derivative memberships and boundary equations among distinct coefficient parameters. A strict witness excludes equality directly. At an equality point the five datum conditions needed for the next block follow from the coefficient-certificate criterion [lem-per-hilbert-boundary-supported-certificates]. This induction allows a block's auxiliary tests to pass through points below the retained level: the chart packet explicitly retains whole-series certificates there. It does not assume that equality upstairs forces equality downstairs.

source.place: BMT arXiv:0905.3580v1 §§5.2,6.1–6.3,6.5–6.6, read at https://arxiv.org/html/0905.3580v1; BM2 Chapter III is the construction reference. Agent structural refinement; archival PDF WANTED. No Stacks tag states this coefficient-chart transport.

proof.text: On each transformed coefficient support in the certificate alternative, apply [lem-per-hilbert-boundary-supported-certificates] to the transported $f_i'$ and its pure forms and whole-series certificates. It gives $H_{K'}\le_{\rm lex}H_{D'}$, equality precisely at the coefficient order conditions $S'$, and supported generation at equality. In the other alternative or off that support, [lem-per-supported-exceptional-chart-packet] supplies $q$ with jet dimensions at most $H_{D'}$ below $q$ and strictly smaller at $q$; this implies strict lexicographic inequality. The Taylor dimension identity [lem-trf-jet-diagram-hilbert-control] identifies these functions with $H_{X_j}$ at arbitrary scheme points, and adjoining $r_j$ free variables gives $H_{D'}=L_j$. Together with the unaffected charts of Step 1 this proves the bound at every prefix. Equality points therefore lie on the coefficient support and satisfy $S'$.

source.place: BMT arXiv:0905.3580v1 §§5.2,6.1–6.3,6.5–6.6, read at https://arxiv.org/html/0905.3580v1; BM2 Chapter III is the construction reference. Agent structural refinement; archival PDF WANTED. No Stacks tag states this coefficient-chart transport.

proof.text: At such an equality point write $A=L[[W,Z]]$ and $K=(f_i)$. The preceding certificate node gives supported generation, and [lem-trf-homogeneous-continuous-formal-division] gives unique division $a=\sum q_if_i+r(a)$ with remainder supported outside $D$. The ideal is exactly the kernel of $r$. All vertices have zero coefficient-variable components. Consequently multiplying a supported division by any coefficient parameter $w$ keeps both quotient and remainder supports allowed; uniqueness gives $r(wa)=w\,r(a)$. More generally for a subset $T$ of coefficient parameters, this makes $r$ linear over the polynomial ring in $T$. Since $r$ is the identity on complement-supported series, it identifies $A/K$ as a module with that space. If $r(a)$ is in $(T)A$, assign each of its monomials to the first parameter of $T$ dividing it; dividing by that parameter keeps the monomial outside $D$. This writes $r(a)$ as a sum of parameters of $T$ times complement-supported series. Hence the module quotient by $T$ consists exactly of complement-supported series with those parameters set to zero. Multiplication by any remaining coefficient parameter is injective by shifting its exponent. The constant monomial survives because every $d_i>0$, including the empty family $K=0$. Thus any ordered subset of distinct coefficient parameters is regular on $A/K$.

proof.text: By the transported chart statement [lem-per-supported-exceptional-chart-packet], the boundary equations at a retained point are precisely such distinct coefficient parameters, up to units and an invertible straightening of the transverse variables. The centered Taylor map is faithfully flat also at nonclosed points by [lem-trf-diagonal-taylor-faithful-flatness]. Contract each ideal $(K,w_1,\ldots,w_s)$ using [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction]: if $w_{s+1}a$ is in that ideal in the stalk, its Taylor image is there, Step 4 puts the image of $a$ there, and contraction puts $a$ there. This proves injectivity in each stalk quotient. The final quotient is nonzero since all boundary equations lie in its maximal ideal; equivalently its formal quotient still contains the constant monomial. Multiplying an equation by a unit changes neither its generated ideal nor injectivity. The definition [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] now gives the asserted regular sequence, for every subset and order. Earlier-center ideals are never inserted into this coordinate list.
